verdict: Sound for a no-block Wild pre-run workflow, but not complete as a current-mechanic registry. HSConfig's contract, drift report, and Wild matrix are broad enough to keep valid Wild decks load-safe while unknown mechanics and future card types stay warning-only, yet live 2026-07-10 HearthstoneJSON data and current Hearthstone expansions still expose modern mechanics that are not explicitly mapped today.
source_backed_evidence: HearthstoneJSON documents that `cards.json` contains every card and that `/v1/latest/` redirects to the latest build, so it remains the right primary machine-readable source for DBF/CardID joins and broad static semantics. Sources: https://hearthstonejson.com/ and https://hearthstonejson.com/docs/cards.html

A live 2026-07-10 probe of `https://api.hearthstonejson.com/v1/latest/enUS/cards.json` returned 35,320 rows and still populated rich static fields such as `heroPowerDbfId` on 2,988 rows, `questReward` on 9 rows, `referencedTags` on 4,494 rows, `spellSchool` on 3,993 rows, and `targetingArrowText` on 1,247 rows.

The same live 2026-07-10 probe showed `entourage` on 0 rows and `playRequirements` on 0 rows, which means current latest HearthstoneJSON is still not a safe single-source authority for generated pools, some targeting constraints, or deeper linked-entity closure by itself.

The same live 2026-07-10 probe showed that latest `cards.json` now includes card types beyond normal Wild deck cards, including `lettuce_ability`, `battleground_trinket`, `battleground_spell`, `battleground_anomaly`, `pet`, and `game_mode_button`, which confirms that future or mode-specific card-type drift is real even when the payload is healthy.

Official Blizzard sources confirm that current and recent Hearthstone still adds or expands mechanics that matter to drift handling: Dredge and Colossal were introduced for Voyage to the Sunken City, Titan and Forge for TITANS, Tourist for Perils in Paradise, Starship for The Great Dark Beyond, Kindred for The Lost City of Un'Goro, and Imbue plus class-wide Choose One cards for Into the Emerald Dream. Sources: https://playhearthstone.com/en-us/blog/23784370/ , https://playhearthstone.com/en-us/expansions-adventures/titans/ , https://playhearthstone.com/en-us/expansions-adventures/perils-in-paradise/ , https://playhearthstone.com/en-us/expansions-adventures/the-great-dark-beyond/ , https://playhearthstone.com/en-us/expansions-adventures/the-lost-city-of-ungoro/ , https://playhearthstone.com/en-gb/blog/24187196/ , https://playhearthstone.com/en-gb/expansions-adventures/into-the-emerald-dream/

A live 2026-07-10 scan of collectible constructed-style cards in latest HearthstoneJSON found current mechanics or markers that are not explicitly registered in HSConfig today, including Kindred, Tourist, Starship, Spellburst, Miniaturize, Quickdraw, Honorable Kill, Elusive, Poisonous, and others; for example, the live scan found `kindred` on 31 texts, `tourist` on 13 texts, `starship` on 8 mechanics plus 49 referenced tags plus 60 texts, `spellburst` on 44 cards, `miniaturize` on 19 cards, and `quickdraw` on 19 cards.

Current Wild meta sources dated July 9-10, 2026 still show broad cross-class archetype diversity rather than one narrow mechanic cluster, including Hand Warlock, Reno Exodia Mage, Odyn Warrior, Broxigar Demon Hunter, Miracle Rogue, Quest Mage, Barnes Druid, Togwaggle Druid, Libram Paladin, Reno Hunter, Cute Warrior, Pirate Warrior, and Even Warlock. Sources: https://hearthstone-decks.net/wild-decks/ , https://www.hsguru.com/meta?format=1

no_block_implications: Unknown mechanics and future card types should remain visible in `mechanic_drift_report.json` and `mechanic_visibility_summary`, but they should not stop `VALID_PACKAGE` or `load_safe_apply` for an otherwise valid Wild deck input.

HearthstoneJSON should stay the primary static card registry for IDs, card text, mechanics, referenced tags, spell school, race data, and structured hero-power or quest metadata, but HSConfig should not assume latest `cards.json` alone can prove generated pools, exact targeting rules, or deeper linked-entity closure.

Because package building scopes drift analysis to deck cards instead of the whole live corpus, mode-specific card-type drift in latest HearthstoneJSON does not currently threaten the normal operator path. That is the correct shape for a no-block Wild workflow.

Mapped mechanics may lower through direct or partial surfaces, but unmapped current mechanics should stay `warning_only` until an exact documented VisionAI surface exists. The system should prefer honest report-only visibility over fabricated runtime rows.

The current Wild matrix is broad enough to justify a load-safe pre-run package promise, but it should be read as representative coverage for common Wild mechanic families, not as proof that every live or newly added keyword has a first-class lowering path.
gaps_or_risks: Live collectible cards still expose current mechanics or markers that HSConfig does not explicitly register today, including Kindred, Tourist, Starship, Spellburst, Miniaturize, Quickdraw, Honorable Kill, Elusive, Poisonous, and others. If a Wild deck depends on one of those signature actions, HSConfig will currently fall back to warning-only or a more generic partial truth instead of a named first-class support row.

The current text-pattern drift detector in C:/Users/darbo/Documents/HSConfig/src/hsconfig/mechanic_drift.py does not yet look for several modern live keywords such as `kindred`, `tourist`, `starship`, `miniaturize`, `quickdraw`, or `spellburst`, so some mechanics may stay less visible than they should unless they also appear in explicit `mechanics`, `referencedTags`, or archetype claims.

Latest HearthstoneJSON still exposes zero `entourage` and zero `playRequirements` rows on 2026-07-10, so any future attempt to broaden support for generated pools, exact play-target rules, or some option/link closures will still need a supplemental deterministic source or a deliberate warning-only boundary.

Latest HearthstoneJSON already contains non-constructed and mode-specific card types. If HSConfig ever repoints drift analysis from deck-card payloads to the whole latest corpus, `unknown_card_types` would become noisy unless the report is explicitly filtered by game mode or supported source scope.

Current Wild meta diversity is real, but no fixed 12-deck matrix can be exhaustive in a format with constant rediscovery and balance changes. Broad coverage is enough for no-block pre-run packaging, not for claiming universal mechanic completeness.
recommended_next_action: Add explicit registry aliases plus text-pattern drift detection for the current live keywords that HSConfig still leaves implicit or unknown, starting with `kindred`, `tourist`, `starship`, `spellburst`, `miniaturize`, `quickdraw`, and `imbue`, and default each to `warning_only` unless an exact documented VisionAI surface already exists.
